Doubtless
dout´lĕs
adv. (without doubt, certainly; rendering the Hebrew oath-formula and infinitive absolute, Greek menounge and ge)
Doubt + less: free of doubt. The Hebrew has no such adverb; the AV supplies it where the Hebrew doubles a verb or swears an oath.

Biblical Definition

Paul: “Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord” (Php 3:8). The psalm of the sower: “He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him” (Psa 126:6). Isaiah's prayer: “Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us” (Isa 63:16). The LORD's oath in the wilderness: “Doubtless ye shall not come into the land… save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun” (Num 14:30). Paul to Corinth: “If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you” (1Co 9:2). David enquiring: “Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand” (2Sa 5:19).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines doubtless as without doubt or question; unquestionably.

expand to see more

DOUBTLESS, a. Free from fear or danger; secure.

DOUBTLESS, adv. Without doubt or question; unquestionably.

Key Scripture

Php 3:8 — "Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ,"

Psa 126:6 — "He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him."

Isa 63:16 — "Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O LORD, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting."

Num 14:30 — "Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun."

1Co 9:2 — "If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord."

Modern Corruption

Doubt is praised as honesty and certainty suspected as pride, and the Bible's doubtless is spoken by God, by a sower, and by an apostle counting his losses.

expand to see more

The age has made a virtue of not being sure. Scripture's doubtless is not the confidence of a man who has never questioned; it is the settled end of a question. Paul's “yea doubtless” comes after he has laid every credential on the table and moved the column; the sower's “shall doubtless come again with rejoicing” is said of a man who went out weeping; Isaiah's “doubtless thou art our father” is prayed by a people whom Abraham would not recognise. Certainty in the Bible is reached through the tears, not around them, and it is not humility to stop short of it. Numbers 14:30 shows the other side: God's doubtless. The oath that the generation would not enter the land was as certain as the promise that Caleb would, and both were kept to the man.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew infinitive absolute (bo yabo, coming he shall come) and the oath-formula im (H518); Greek menounge (G3304), yea rather, doubtless; ge (G1065), at least, indeed.

expand to see more

Hebrew bo yabo (H935 doubled) — he shall surely come; Psalm 126:6; im (H518) in an oath, “doubtless ye shall not”; Numbers 14:30; ki (H3588), Isaiah 63:16.

Greek menounge (G3304) — yea doubtless; Philippians 3:8; ge (G1065), 1 Corinthians 9:2.

Usage

"“Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss” — certainty after the reckoning."

"“Shall doubtless come again with rejoicing” — said of a man who went out weeping."

"“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land” — God's certainty, kept to the man."
